Name: Clark Field
Address: Stotsenburg Park, Emilio Aguinaldo Street, Clark Freeport, Mabalacat, Pampanga
Inscription Photo: height: 3335; file: Clark Field (Fort Stotsenburg) historical marker.jpg; credit: Roel Balingit {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; width: 2627
Location Photo: file: 0520jfFort Stotsenburg Parkfvf 18.JPG; credit: Judgefloro {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; width: 4608; height: 3456
Wikipedia Articles: Fort Stotsenburg: true; Clark Air Base: true; Clark Freeport and Special Economic Zone: true
Inscription Tl: Dating pati o pamayanan ng mga Aeta. Naging Camp Stotsenburg bilang paggunita kay Col. John Miller Stotsenburg ng 1st Nebraska Regiment, 1902. Lupang-laan para sa hukbo ng Estados Unidos, 1 Setyembre 1903. Nagtayo ng paliparan at tinawag na Clark Field bilang paggunita sa pilotong si Maj. Harold Merville Clar, 1919. Sinalakay ng mga Hapon, 8 Disyembre 1941. Pook ng labanan ng mga sundalong Amerikano, Pilipino at Hapon, 1945. Nanatili sa pamamahala ng Estados Unidos ayon sa kasunduang base militar ng RP–US, 1947. Clark Air Force Base, 1949. Isinara, 1991. Naging Clark Special Economic Zone, 1992.

Name: Lazaro Francisco
Address: Lazaro Francisco Elementary School, Zulueta Street, Cabanatuan, Nueva Ecija
Inscription Photo: width: 3096; file: Lazaro Francisco historical marker.jpg; credit: Carlo Joseph Moskito {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; height: 4128
Inscription Tl: Makabayan, pangunahing nobelista sa Panitikang Pilipino. Isinilang sa Orani, Bataan, Pebrero 22, 1898. Lumaki sa Cabanatuan at nagsulat ng nobela sa bayang ito mula 1925. Mahalagang bahagi ng kanyang panulat ang pakikisangkot sa mga suliraning tumutukoy sa kapakanan ng bansa. Tagapagtatag ng Kapatiran ng mga Alagad ng Wikang Pilipino (KAWIKA), 1958. Tampok sa mga tinanggap niyang gawad: Republic Cultural Heritage Award, 1970; Patnubay ng Kalinangan, Maynila, 1975; Dangal ng Lahi, Lungsod ng Quezon, 1976; Tanglaw ng Lahi, Ateneo de Manila, 1979. Sa kanyang alaala ang Cabanatuan West Central School ay pinangalanan noong 1987 ng “Paaralang Elementaryang Lazaro Francisco.” Namatay noong Hunyo 17, 1980.

Name: Death Place of General Antonio Luna
Address: College of the Immaculate Conception, Del Pilar Street, Cabanatuan, Nueva Ecija
Title En: Death Place of General Antonio Luna
Inscription En: On the plaza, in front of this building, formerly the Presidential Headquarters of the First Philippine Republic, General Antonio Luna and his aide Colonel Francisco Roman were assasinated in the afternoon of 5 June 1899, by members of General Emilio Aguinaldo’s presidential guard.
Inscription Photo: height: 4128; file: Death Place of General Antonio Luna Historical Marker.jpg; credit: Carlo Joseph Moskito {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; width: 3096

Name: Bahay ni Angel Pantaleon de Miranda
Address: Angel Pantaleon de Miranda House, 770 Santo Rosario Street, Angeles
Inscription Photo: width: 2942; credit: Roel Balingit {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; file: Angel Pantaleon de Miranda House historical marker (cropped).jpg; height: 3718
Title Tl: Bahay ni Angel Pantaleon de Miranda
Inscription Tl: Ipinatayong yari sa bato at kahoy noong 1824 ni Don Angel Pantaleon de Miranda at kanyang maybahay, Doña Rosalia de Jesus, ang nagtatag ng Angeles (Dating Culiat), Pampanga noong 1796. Minana ng kanilang anak na si Doña Juana Miranda de Henson at pagkaraan ay tinirahan ng mga tagapagmana ni Don Jose P. Henson. Kasalukuyang tahanan ni Don Vicente N. Henson, Sr. Naging tuluyan din ng hukbong rebolusyonaryo ni Hen. Emilio Aguinaldo noong panahon ng Digmaaang Pilipino–Amerikano, 1899.

Name: Aurora Aragon Quezon
Address: Rizal Street cor. San Luis Street, Baler, Aurora
Inscription Photo: file: Aurora Aragon Quezon Historical Marker.jpg; credit: Ervin Malicdem {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; width: 1547; height: 2063
Location Photo: width: 3264; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: Aurorahousejf.JPG; height: 2448
Inscription Tl:
Lider Sibika at pangunang unang ginang ng bansa sa ilalim ng malasariling pamahalaan ng Pilipinas. Ipinanganak noong ika-19 ng Pebrero 1888 sa Baler, Tayabas (ngayo’y sakop ng lalawigan ng Aurora). Nag-aral sa Paaralang Normal ng Pilipinas. Ikinasal sa Hongkong kay Manuel Luis Quezon, Pangulo ng Senado noong 1918. Mga anak: Maria Aurora, Maria Zeneida, Luisa Corazon Paz at Manuel L., Jr.

Nagtatag at nagsagawa ng iba’t-ibang batayan ng kaalaman para sa mamamayan, lalo na ng kabataan, sa Baler upang mapaunlad ang karunungang bumasa’t sumulat at maitaguyod ang mga tungkuling pambayan. Makaraang mamatay ang Pangulong Quezon (1944) nagtaguyod ng mga gawaing panlipunan at panrelihiyon para mapabuti ang pamantayan ng pamumuhay at pagbibigay ng karunungan at biyaya sa mga kapuspalad. Namuno para makilalang isang pambansang samahan ang Krus na Pula at naging unang babaeng pangulo nito. Tinangkilik ang pagtatayong-muli ng makasaysayang simbahan ng Baler.

Habang pauwi ng Baler, tinambangan ng isang pangkat ng Hukbalahap sa Nueva Ecija at kasamang napatay si Maria Aurora, manugang na Felipe Buencamino III at ilang kaibigan noong ika-28 ng Abril 1949.

Bilang parangal sa kanya, itinatag ang sub-lalawigan ng Aurora noong 1951 sa pamamagitan ng Batas ng Republika Blg. 648 at ginawang lalawigan ito sa bisa ng Batas Pambansa Blg. 7 noong 1978.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on a concrete mounting outside Aurora Aragon’s replica house.

Name: Bayan ng Baler
Address: Baler Municipal Hall, San Luis Street, Baler, Aurora
Inscription Photo: width: 996; credit: Ervin Malicdem {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; file: Baler Historical Marker.jpg; height: 1471
Inscription Tl: Lumang pamayanan sa barrio Sabang, bago dumating ang mga Espanyol. Itinatag bilang misyon ng mga paring Pransiskano, 1609. Nasira ng malalaking alon, 27 Disyembre 1735. Lumikas pansamantala ang mga mamamayan sa burol ng Ermita bago lumipat sa kasalukuyang pook. Naging kabisera ng distrito ng El Principe (ngayo’y Aurora), 1856. Pook na sinilangan ni Manuel Luis Quezon, 19 Agosto 1878. Sumiklab ang himagsikan, Oktubre 1897. Naganap sa simbahan ang pagkubkob ng mga rebolusyonaryo sa puwersang Espanyol, 27 Hunyo 1898 – 2 Hunyo 1899, na kinilala bilang mga kaibigan ng bisa ng dekreto ni Hen. Emilio Aguinaldo, 20 Hunyo 1899. Naging bahagi ng Tayabas (ngayo’y Quezon), 12 Hunyo 1902. Naging kabisera ng sub-province ng Aurora, 1951, at ng lalawigan ng Aurora, 1979.

Name: Church of Lubao
Address: Lubao Church, Lubao, Pampanga
Inscription En: Founded 1572 in Barrio Santa Catalina. Moved to this site thirty years later due to yearly floods. Architect Fr. Antonio Herrera, Augustinian, constructed this church 1614–1630 out of locally-made brick and sand mixed in egg albumen contributed by the people of Lubao. Occupied 1898 by the revolutionists. Used as hospital 1899 by American forces. Destroyed 1942 by Japanese shelling. Repaired 1949–1952, under the direction of Fr. Melencio Garcia and other priests.
Inscription Photo: height: 3766; width: 2400; file: Church of Lubao historical marker.jpg; credit: Photo: Judgefloro; perspective correction: Eugene Alvin Villar (seav)
Location Photo: height: 1857; width: 3180; file: Lubao Church lower-left facade.jpg; credit: Judgefloro
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the church facade to the left of the main entrance.

Name: Church of Barasoain
Address: Barasoain Church, Paseo del Congreso cor. Don Antonio Bautista Street, Malolos, Bulacan
Inscription En: Barasoain was originally part of Malolos until its official separation on August 31, 1859. In 1903 it became part of Malolos again. The old Church constructed by Rev. Francisco Royo, O.S.A., was destroyed by fire in May, 1884, but rebuilt by Rev. Juan Giron, O.S.A., in 1885. This Church was the seat of the Revolutionary Congress which convened from the middle of September, 1898, to the last week of February, 1899, under the presidency of Pedro A. Paterno. Among the important measures passed by the Congress was the Malolos Constitution, drafted chiefly by Felipe G. Calderon.
Inscription Photo: height: 2000; width: 1989; file: Philippines Historical Committee Marker for Barasoain Church.JPG; credit: Cool2compute {CC BY‑SA 3.0}
Location Photo: height: 603; width: 877; credit: Shubert Ciencia {CC BY 2.0}; file: Historical markers on the facade of Barasoain Church.jpg
Wikipedia Articles: Malolos Constitution: true; Barasoain Church: true; Malolos Congress: true
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the wall to the left of the central main door of the church.

Name: Simbahan ng Barasoain
Address: Barasoain Church, Paseo del Congreso cor. Don Antonio Bautista Street, Malolos, Bulacan
Inscription Photo: width: 2500; credit: Photo: Judgefloro; perspective correction: Eugene Alvin Villar (seav); file: Simbahan ng Barasoain historical marker.jpg; height: 2255
Location Photo: height: 603; width: 877; credit: Shubert Ciencia {CC BY 2.0}; file: Historical markers on the facade of Barasoain Church.jpg
Inscription Tl: Sa bisa ng Kautusan ng Pangulo Bilang 260, Agosto 1, 1973 na sinusugan ng Kautusan Bilang 375, Enero 14, 1974, ang simbahang ito ay ipinahayag na Pambansang Palatandaang Makasaysayan.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the wall to the left of the southern main door of the church.

Name: Ang Bayan ng Obando
Address: J. P. Rizal Street, Obando, Bulacan
Inscription Photo: height: 4608; width: 3456; file: Ang Bayan ng Obando Historical marker.jpg; credit: Judgefloro
Location Photo: height: 3456; width: 4608; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: Fertilityobandojf.JPG
Inscription Tl: Unang nakilala sa tawag na Baryo Catangalan sakop ng Meycawayan. Naging sakop ng Polo nang ang huli ay humiwalay sa Meycawayan noong 1623. Naging bayan ng Obando noong Mayo 14, 1753, sa bisa ng kautusang inilagda ni Gobernador Heneral Jose Francisco de Obando y Solis. Lubusang nahiwalay sa bayan ng Polo noong 1754 nang sang-ayunan ang pagiging bayan nito nina Francisco Morales y Mozarabe, gobernador ng Lalawigang Bulakan at Kamahal-mahalang Reberendo Alejandro Ferrer, ministrong panlalawigan. Si Padre Manuel de Olivencia ang unang kura paroko at si Diego San Diego ang naging unang alkalde. Ang kapistahan ay tuwing ika 17–18 ng Mayo.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the concrete pedestal commemorating the Obando Fertility Dance Festival in front of Obando Municipal Hall.

Name: Bulacan Military Area
Address: Gen. Alejo G. Santos Highway, Poblacion, Bustos, Bulacan
Inscription Photo: height: 681; file: BMA HistoricalMarker Bustos.jpg; credit: Ryomaandres {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; width: 465
Location Photo: height: 4608; credit: Judgefloro; file: FvfBustosBulacan0325 02.JPG; width: 3456
Inscription Tl: Binuo sa ilalim ng East Central Luzon Guerilla Area (ECLGA) ang Bulacan Military District mula sa apat na rehimento ng puwersang gerilya na kumakatawan sa lalawigan ng Bulacan sa utos ni Maj. Edwin P. Ramsey, 14 Setyembre 1943. Capt. Alejo S. Santos, District Commander. Pinangalanang Bulacan Military Area ni Capt. Bernard L. Anderson ng USAFFE Luzon Guerilla Armed Forces, 21 Disyembre 1943. Ang apat na rehimento ng BMA ay naging sampung rehimento, 1944. Tumulong sa pakikipaglaban sa puwersang Hapon sa mga lalawigan ng Nueva Vizcaya, Pangasinan, Pampanga, Ifugao, at Rizal. Nakipaglaban sa mga Hapones hanggang mapalaya sa mga Hapon ang lalawigan ng Bulacan, Hulyo 1945.

Name: Church of Meycauayan
Address: Meycauayan Church, Marcos Ira Street, Meycauayan, Bulacan
Inscription En: The first Church was destroyed by a typhoon in 1588. The construction of the present Church was started shortly after 1668, when the town was moved from Lagolo to the present site. Rev. Francisco Gascueña, O.F.M., who built the belfry in 1800, preached the Gospel in China for six years, and on being exiled from that kingdom out of opposition to his religious teachings returned to Meycauayan. He served this parish for 31 years and died here on November 18, 1831. The Convent was built from 1731 to 1759. Both Convent and Church were seriously damaged by the typhoon of 1882.
Inscription Photo: width: 3006; credit: Robby dela vega {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; file: PHC-installed historical marker for Meycauayan Church.jpg; height: 3626
Location Photo: height: 3456; file: MeycauayanChurchBulacan 08.JPG; credit: Judgefloro; width: 4608
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the wall on the westernmost portion of the church facade.

Name: Birthplace of General Gregorio H. del Pilar
Address: Birthplace of General Gregorio del Pilar Historical Landmark, Camino Real Street, Bulakan, Bulacan
Title En: Birthplace of General Gregorio H. del Pilar
Inscription En: Site in the town of Bulacan where General Gregorio H. del Pilar was born November 14, 1875. Fifth child of Ferrnando H. del Pilar and Felipa Sempio. Intrepid, valiant and youngest Filipino General. Figured most prominently in the defense of Kakaron, Attack of Paombong, Liberation of Bulacan, and in the Battle of Tirad Pass where he died “a soldier and a gentleman,” December 2, 1899.
Inscription Photo: width: 1686; credit: Photo: Judgefloro; perspective correction: Eugene Alvin Villar (seav); file: Birthplace of General Gregorio H. del Pilar historical marker.jpg; height: 2846
Location Photo: height: 4608; width: 3456; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: Gregoriojf.JPG
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the pedestal for the statue of del Pilar.

Name: Birthplace of Marcelo H. del Pilar
Address: Marcelo H. del Pilar Shrine, Barangay San Nicolas Street, Bulakan, Bulacan
Title En: Birthplace of Marcelo H. del Pilar
Inscription En: Born in Barrio San Nicolas, town of Bulacan on August 30, 1850 to Julian H. del Pilar and Blasa Gatmaytan. Marcelo H. del Pilar, patriot, writer and editor of La Solidaridad, a newspaper of the Propaganda Movement published in Spain. Died in Barcelona, July 4, 1896.
Inscription Photo: width: 2586; file: JC Marcelo Shrine 16.JPG; credit: JJ Carpio {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; height: 3636

Name: Simbahan ng Quingua
Address: Santiago Apostol Church, Gov. Padilla Road cor. P. Vergel de Dios Street, Plaridel, Bulacan
Inscription Photo: credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: Quinga Church historical marker.jpg; width: 3456; height: 4608
Location Photo: height: 3456; file: 03121jfWeddings at the Santiago Apostol Church Plaridel 2017fvf 34.jpg; credit: Judgefloro; width: 4608
Wikipedia Articles: Santiago Apostol Church: Santiago Apostol Church (Plaridel)
Inscription Tl: Ito ang kauna-unahang simbahang itinayo sa Lumang Bayan ng mga paring Agustino sa pamahala ni Reb. P. Pedro Vasquez nang mga taong 1580–1595. Inilipat dito sa kabayanan noong 1605 sa pamamahala ni Reb. P. Diego Pardo. Muling ipinaayos nang taong 1722. Ang kauna-unahang kura parokong Pilipino ay si Reb. P. Victorino Lopez, na sumama sa kilusan ng Himagsikan, bilang isang pinuno, sa ilalim ni Kapitan Jose Serapio ng Santa Maria. Ang simbahan at kumbento ay ginawang pagamutang hukbo at kuwartel ng mga Amerikano, 1899.

Name: Church of Balanga
Address: Balanga Cathedral, Aguirre Street cor. J.P. Rizal Street, Balanga, Bataan
Inscription En: The spiritual ministration of Balanga formerly belonged to Abucay. Balanga became an independent missionary center in 1739. Rev. Benito Rivas, O.P., strengthened this church by fortifying its wall. Rev. Juan Antonio Vicente, O.P., roofed it with galvanized iron and decorated the interior. Rev. Fernaldo Ma. Miñano, O.P., from 1838–45 constructed the arch of the choir loft and made the baptismal font out of granite from Mariveles. The parochial ministration under the Filipino clergy started with Rev. Mariano Sarili, June 2, 1898.
Inscription Photo: file: Church of Balanga historical marker.jpg; credit: Photo: Ramon FVelasquez; perspective correction and retouching: Eugene Alvin Villar (seav) {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; width: 2500; height: 2787

Name: Nicanor Abelardo at Sta. Ana
Address: 146 Payawal Street, San Miguel, Bulacan
Inscription Tl:
Isinilang si Nicanor Abelardo sa pook na ito ng San Miguel, Bulakan, noong ika-7 ng Pebrero, 1893, anak na panganay nina Valentin Abelardo at Placida Sta. Ana. Nagtapos ng musika sa Unibersidad ng Pilipinas noong 1921 at sa Chicago Musical College noong 1932. Sa bisa ng kanyang matitimyas na kundiman at mga himig na naglalarawan ng katutubong tanawin, si Abelardo ay tinaguriang “Makata ng Tugtugin” at kinikilalang pinakadakilang mangangatha ng tugtugin sa Pilipinas. Sa kanyang mga tugtugin ay lalong natampok ang “Nasaan ka Irog” at “Mutya ng Pasig.”

Yumao noong ika-21 ng Marso, 1934, sa Maynila.

Name: Dr. Maximo Viola
Address: Cagayan Valley Road cor. Viola Street, San Miguel, Bulacan
Inscription En:
Here in Barrio Sta. Rita, San Miguel, Bulacan, was born Maximo Viola, friend and traveling companion in Europe of Jose Rizal, who advanted the money needed for the printing of Rizal’s novel NOLI ME TANGERE.

Dr. Viola and Dr. Rizal toured Europe together, May–June, 1887, visiting various cities in Germany, Austria, Hungary and Switzerland. One of the places they visited was Leitmeritz, Austria, hometown of Professor Ferdinand Blumentritt.
Inscription Photo: height: 4608; width: 3456; credit: Judgefloro; file: Maximo Viola historical marker.jpg
Location Photo: height: 4608; width: 3456; file: FvfBulacan8172 15.JPG; credit: Judgefloro
Location Description: The historical marker is mounted on a concrete pedestal beside the road.

Name: Simon Tecson
Address: Rizal Street, San Miguel, Bulacan
Inscription Photo: height: 4608; width: 3456; credit: Judgefloro; file: Simon Tecson historical marker in San Miguel, Bulacan.jpg
Location Photo: width: 4608; credit: Judgefloro; file: FvfTecsonHouse7000 14.JPG; height: 3456
Inscription Tl: Koronel ng Hukbong Rebolusyonaryo sa Bulacan. Isinilang sa San Miguel de Mayumo, Bulacan, 5 Pebrero 1861. Lumagda sa Konstitusyon ng Biyak-na-Bato, 1897. Inatasan ni Hen. Emilio Aguinaldo na pamunuan ang pagkubkob ng puwersang Espanyol sa Simbahan ng Baler (ngayo’y sakop ng lalawigan ng Aurora), 1899. Lumagda sa kasunduan ng pagsuko ng mga Espanyol sa pangunguna ni Martin Cerezo, 2 Hunyo 1899. Lumaban sa Digmaang Filipino–Amerikano, 1899; sumuko, 12 Pebrero 1901. Ipinatapon sa Guam dulot ng hindi pagkilala sa pamahalaang Amerikano, 16 Hunyo 1901; nakabalik sa Pilipinas, Setyembre 1902. Yumao, 15 Nobyembre 1903.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the pillar immediately to the left of the main entrance gate to the property.

Name: Ang Simbahan ng Bulacan
Address: Our Lady of Assumption Church, Bulakan, Bulacan
Inscription Photo: width: 1920; credit: JJ Carpio {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; file: Bulacan Church historical marker.jpg; height: 2880
Wikipedia Articles: Our Lady of Assumption Church: Our Lady of Assumption Church (Bulakan)
Inscription Tl: Itinatag ng mga paring Agustino bilang visita ng Tondo, 1575. Ipinatayo ang simbahang parokyal at kumbento sa patronato ng Nuestra Señora de la Asuncion, 1578. Sinakop at sinunog ng mga Ingles, 1762. Muling ipinatayo, 1812. Ipinagawa ang kampanaryo, 1877. Nasira ng lindol, 1863, 1869, at 1880. Ipinaayos sa disenyong Neo-Byzantine, 1884–1885. Natapos ang kampanaryo, 1889. Dito lihim na ipinamahagi ni Gregorio H. del Pilar ang mga polyeto sa panulat ng kanyang amaing si Marcelo H. del Pilar noong panahon ng Propaganda laban sa mga Kastila. Ipinanumbalik at ipinaayos ang simbahan, 1955–1975.

Name: Capas Concentration Camp
Address: Capas National Shrine, Km. 112 Tarlac–Zambales Road, Brgy. Aranguren, Capas, Tarlac
Inscription Photo: credit: Photo: Ramon FVelasquez; perspective correction: Eugene Alvin Villar (seav) {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: Capas Concentratrion Camp historical marker.jpg; width: 2438; height: 3226
Wikipedia Articles: Capas National Shrine: true; Camp O'Donnell: true
Inscription Tl: Itinatag noong 1940 bilang Camp O’Donnell. Nagsilbing bilangguan ng mahigit na 40,000 kawal Pilipino at 9,000 kawal Amerikano na bihag ng digma na dumanas ng Death March. Humigit-kumulang sa 30,000 ang namatay sa kampong ito sanhi ng sakit at ibayong pahirap mula Abril hanggang Hunyo 1942. Inilibing sa iisang hukay ang mga nasawing bayani. Nakilala sa pangalang Capas Concentration Camp. Naging bahagi ng Clark Air Base Military Reservation makaraan ang Ikalawang Digmaang Pandaigdig. Ibinalik sa Republika ng Pilipinas 9 Abril 1982. Ipinahayag na isang Pambansang Dambana 9 Oktubre 1991.
Location Description: The historical marker is attached to the base of one of the legs of the obelisk-like structure.

Name: Death March
Address: Capas, Tarlac
Inscription En: At this railroad station of Capas, the Filipino and American prisoners of war who survived the horrendous trip from San Fernando, during which so many smothered to death in the densely crowded cars, were unloaded and force, although on the point of collapse to march the 6 kilometers to Camp O’Donnell, where they were concentrated.
Inscription Photo: width: 2500; credit: Photo: Judgefloro; perspective correction: Eugene Alvin Villar (seav); file: Death March April 1942 historical marker.jpg; height: 2810
Location Photo: height: 3456; file: 002jfSanto Domingo Death March Marker Capas Tarlacfvf 07.JPG; credit: Judgefloro; width: 4608
Inscription Tl: Sa himpilang daang-bakal na ito ng Capas, ang mga bihag ng digmang kawal Pilipino at Amerikano na himalang nakaligtas sa makahayup na paglalakbay mula San Fernando, ay muling pinaglakad gayong mga nag-aagaw buhay, hanggang Kampo O’Donnell na may 6 kilometro ang layo. Sa impiyernong kulungang yaon, sila’y naging bilanggo.
Location Description: The historical marker is attached to a large white triangular-shaped stone at Kilometer 106 of the Death March route.

Name: The Fall of Bataan
Address: Bataan Provincial Capitol, Capitol Drive, Balanga, Bataan
Inscription En: [The fall of Bataan] sealed in blood the permanent ties of friendship and cooperation between the Philippines and the United States. This marker is dedicated, 9 April 1952, to the memory of the gallant Filipino and Americans soldiers as well as civilians, who fought and died side by side in the defense of Democracy.
Inscription Photo: width: 2500; credit: Photo: Ramon FVelasquez; perspective correction: Eugene Alvin Villar (seav) {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: The Fall of Bataan historical marker.jpg; height: 3641
Location Photo: width: 600; credit: National Historical Commission of the Philippines; file: The Fall of Bataan historical marker 02.jpg; height: 450

Name: Tomas Guillermo T. del Rosario
Address: Bataan Provincial Capitol, Capitol Drive, Balanga, Bataan
Inscription Photo: credit: Photo: Ramon FVelasquez; perspective correction: Eugene Alvin Villar (seav) {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: Tomas Guillermo T. del Rosario historical marker.jpg; width: 2500; height: 3751
Inscription Tl: Masigasig na tagapagtaguyod ng karapatan sa malayang pagsamba at ng pagkakahiwalay ng simbahan at estado. Isinilang kina Cipriano del Rosario at Severina Tongco sa Binondo, Maynila, 10 Pebrero 1857. Nagtapos ng Bachiller en Artes sa Ateneo Municipal, 1875; at Licenciado en Derecho sa Unibersidad ng Santos Tomas, 1886. Naglingkod bilang juez de paz, promotor fiscal, at juez de primera instancia ng Maynila, 1888–1896. Ipinatapon sa Cueta, Aprika sa pagkakasangkot sa himagsikan 1896–1897. Nagbalik sa Pilipinas at nahirang sa delegado sa Kongreso ng Malolos bilang kinatawan ng Surigao, 1898. Nahalal na gobernador ng Bataan, 1904–1906; at kinatawan sa Philippine Assembly, 1909–1912. Yumao, 4 Hulyo 1913.

Name: Diosdado P. Macapagal
Address: President Diosdado P. Macapagal Library and Museum, Lubao, Pampanga
Inscription En:
5th President of the Republic of the Philippines, a native son of Lubao, Pampanga, with deliberate patience, liberated himself from and transcended all the shackling obstacles adherent to the poverty of his birth on September 28, 1910.

Working his way through school, partly with the support of philantrophist Honorio Ventura, he earned the degrees of Bachelor of Laws, Master of Laws, Doctor of Laws and Doctor of Economics from the University of Santo Tomas. He topped the bar examination in 1936.

In 1949, he was elected Congressman for the first district of Pampanga, after two terms in Congress, he was elected Vice President of the Philippines in 1957 and was chosen as President of the Liberal Party. In 1961, he was elected President of the Republic of the Philippines.

As President, he had two objectives: to fight mass poverty and to strengthen and maturize democracy in the Philippines. On August 8, 1963, he enacted the Agricultural Land Reform Code, which abolished the centuries-old tenancy in the Philippines. After his retirement from politics in 1965, he was elected delegate to the 1971 Constitutional Convention which elected him as its president.

Diosdado Macapagal’s service to his people and country is characterized by his personal virtues of honesty, commitment and integrity and by a deep love and fear of God. All these manifestations of his idealism are shared by his wife, Evangelina Macaraeg-Macapagal, and his children Cielo Macapagal-Salgado, Arturo Macapagal, Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo and Diosdado Macapagal, Jr.

Location Photo: height: 4608; width: 3456; credit: Judgefloro; file: Diosdado Macapagal historical marker in Lubao.jpg
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the pedestal holding the bust of Macapagal.

Name: Ang Bahay na Sinilangan ni Pangulong Diosdado Macapagal
Address: President Diosdado P. Macapagal Library and Museum, Lubao, Pampanga
Inscription Photo: width: 3456; file: AbDiosdado Macapagal.JPG; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; height: 4608
Title Tl: Ang Bahay na Sinilangan ni Pangulong Diosdado Macapagal
Inscription Tl: Sa bahay na itong yari sa pawid at kawayan, ang panglimang naging pangulo ng Republika ng Pilipinas Diosdado Macapagal ay ipinanganak noong ika-28 ng Setyembre 1910. Pangalawa sa apat na anak nina Urbano Macapagal at Romana Pangan. Dito niya ginugol ang mga masasayang unang taon ng kanyang kabataan. Ang pagsasaayos na muli ng bahay na ito ay isinagawa sa pagtutulungan ng mga mamamayan ng Lubao, ng Pamahalaan at ng Kagawaran ng Edukasyon, Kultura at Isports (Rehiyon III).

Name: Himpilang Daang-bakal ng San Fernando
Address: San Fernando station, San Fernando, Pampanga
Inscription Photo: credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: San Fernando Pampanga train station historical marker.jpg; width: 3456; height: 4608
Location Photo: width: 4608; file: San Fernando Pampanga train station.jpg; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; height: 3456
Wikipedia Articles: San Fernando station: San Fernando station (Pampanga)
Inscription Tl: Itinayo noong 1892 bilang bahagi ng linyang Manila–Dagupan ng Manila Railroad Company. Dito bumaba si Jose Rizal nang dalawin niya ang San Fernando. Sa himpilang daang-bakal ding ito, noong Abril 1942, isinakay sa tren ang mga bihag na sundalong kasama sa Death March patungo sa Kampo O’Donnell, Capas, Tarlac, upang doon ikulong.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the facade to the left of the street entrance of the station.

Name: Lalawigan ng Pampanga
Address: Governor Macario Arnedo Park, Capitol Boulevard, San Fernando, Pampanga
Inscription Photo: height: 4260; width: 3144; file: NHI Province of Pampanga historical marker.jpg; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}
Location Photo: height: 4160; width: 3120; credit: Roel Balingit {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; file: Pampanga Provincial Capitol flag pole base and historical marker.jpg
Inscription Tl: Pinanahanan ng mga Indo–Malayo ang dakong itaas na pampang, ang pook ay ginalugad ng mga paring Agustino noong 1571. Naging encomienda noong 1576. Dahil pinakamaunlad, pinakamaganda at pinakamasagana, ito ay naging tagatustos ng bigas noong panahon ng Kastila. Nag-alsa laban sa pagmamamlupit ng mga Kastila, minsan noong ika-16 na dantaon at tatlong ulit noong ika-17 dantaon. Ang mga Pampango ay pinangunahan ni Francisco Maniago sa isang nasasandatahang pag-aalsa laban sa sapilitang paggawa at labis-labis na pagpataw ng buwis. Isinalin ang 8 bayan nito sa Bataan, 5 sa Nuweba Esiha at 4 sa Tarlak (na ibinalik pagkaraan). Ang Bakolor ay naging kabisera ng Pilipinas sa ilalim ng Espanya noong 1762–64. Noong panahon ng Amerikano, ang unang pamahalaang sibil ay itinatag sa lalawigan na binubuo ng 22 bayan noong Pebrero 13, 1901. Ang San Fernando ay naging kabisera noong 1904. Masidhing pakikipaglaban ng mga Pampango sa Hapon ang naranasan noong Ikalawang Digmaang Pandaigdig. Ang pinakamalaking himpilan ng Hukbong Panghimpapawid ng Amerika sa Asya ay matatapuan sa Lungsod ng Angeles.
Location Description: The historical marker is located at the flag pole base across the capitol building.

Name: Maximino H. Hizon
Address: Governor Macario Arnedo Park, Capitol Boulevard, San Fernando, Pampanga
Inscription Photo: width: 2447; credit: Roel Balingit {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; file: Maximino Hizon historical marker.jpg; height: 3606
Location Photo: file: Gen. Maximo Hizon Statue at Pampanga Capitol.png; credit: Artgigster {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; width: 1017; height: 780
Inscription Tl: Heneral ng Himagsikan, kagawad ng Kongreso ng Malolos at makabayan. Ipinanganak sa Parian, Mexico, Pampanga noong Mayo 9, 1870. Umanib sa Katipunan, 1896. Dinakip at ipinatapon sa Jolo nang matuklasan ang lihim na samahan noong Agosto 19, 1896. Pinalaya pagkaraang lagdaan ang Kasunduan sa Biak-na-Bato. Hinirang na Komandante Heneral ng Pampanga at pagkaraan brigadyer heneral, 1898. Hinirang na kinatawan ng lalawigan ng Sorsogon sa Kongreso ng Malolos. Naging kilala sa madugong labanan sa Caloocan noong Pebrero 23, 1899, at sa mga pagsalakay sa mga pangkat ng Amerikano hindi lamang sa Pampanga kungdi sa Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac at Pangasinan. Nasugatan sa labanan sa Dumandan. Malapit sa Porac noong Enero 17, 1900, nabihag sa San Jose, Malino, Mexico noong Hunyo 19, 1900. Ipinatapon sa Guam na pook na na kanyang kinamatayan noong Setyembre 1, 1901.
Location Description: The historical marker is located in front of the Maximino Hizon monument at the central section of the Gov. Macario Arnedo Park in front of the Capitol building.

Name: Jose Abad Santos
Address: Governor Macario Arnedo Park, Capitol Boulevard, San Fernando, Pampanga
Inscription Photo: height: 3180; credit: Roel Balingit {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; file: Jose Abad Santos historical marker (Pampanga Capitol).jpg; width: 2599
Location Photo: width: 4608; file: Jose Abad Santos Monument (Pampanga Capitol).jpg; credit: Judgefloro; height: 3456
Inscription Tl: Dalubhasa sa batas, estadista, makabayan, martir. Ipinanganak sa San Fernando, Pampanga, 19 Pebrero 1886. Itinalaga bilang kinatawan ng Pangulo ng Komonwelt ng Pilipinas noong mga unang araw ng pananakop ng mga Hapon. Binaril sa Malabang, Lanao, 2 Mayo 1942, dahil sa pagtangging manumpa ng katapatan sa Imperyong Hapon.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the monument base of Jose Abad Santos at the eastern section of the Gov. Macario Arnedo Park in front of the Capitol building.

Name: Diosdado Macapagal
Address: Pampanga Provincial Capitol, Capitol Boulevard, San Fernando, Pampanga
Inscription Photo: height: 3827; width: 2538; credit: Roel Balingit {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; file: Diosdado Macapagal historical marker (Pampanga Capitol).jpg
Location Photo: credit: Roel Balingit {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; file: Diosdado Macapagal monument (Pampanga Capitol).jpg; width: 3120; height: 4160
Inscription Tl: Ika-9 na Pangulo ng Republika ng Pilipinas, 1961–1965. Isinilang sa San Nicolas, Lubao, Pilipinas, 28 Setyembre 1910. Nagtapos ng Associate in Arts sa Unibersidad ng Pilipinas, 1932, abogasya (1936), Master of Laws (1941), Doctor of Civil Law (1947); at Doctor of Economics (1957) sa Unibersidad ng Santo Tomas. Unang pangulo ng Philippine Lawyers Association, 1947. Kinatawan ng unang distrito ng Pampanga sa Pangalawa at Pangatlong Kongreso ng Pilipinas, 1949–1957; may akda ng Foreign Service Act ng 1952. Pangalawang Pangulo ng Pilipinas, 1957–1961; Pangulo ng Liberal Party, 1958–1961; 1964–1966. Itinakda ang pagdiriwang ng Araw ng Kalayaan ng Pilipinas tuwing ika-12 ng Hunyo, 1964. Nagpasimula ng pagtatatag ng MAPHILINDO upang palakasin ang ugnayan ng Malaysia, Philippines at Indonesia, 1963; nilagdaan ang Agricultural Land Reform Code, 1963. Pangulo ng 1971 Constitutional Convention. Ama ni Gloria Macapagal Arroyo, ika-14 na Pangulo ng Republika ng Pilipinas (2004–2010). Yumao, 21 Abril 1997.
Location Description: The historical marker is installed upright in front the Diosdado Macapagal monument located to the left of the main entrance of the capitol building.

Name: Benigno S. Aquino, Jr. “Ninoy”
Address: Pampanga Provincial Capitol, Capitol Boulevard, San Fernando, Pampanga
Inscription Photo: width: 2389; file: Benigno Aquino Jr. historical marker (Pampanga Capitol).jpg; credit: Roel Balingit {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; height: 3507
Location Photo: height: 3456; width: 4608; file: Ninoy Aquino Monument and marker at the Pampanga Provincial Capitol.jpg; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}
Inscription Tl: Isinilang sa Concepcion, Tarlac, 27 Nobyembre 1932. Cub reporter, The Manila Times, 1949. Correspondent sa Digmaan sa Korea, 1950–1951. Ginawaran ng Philippine Legion of Honor ni Elpidio R. Quirino, 1951; at Pangulong Ramon F. Magsaysay, 1954. Negosyador sa muling pagsailalim sa batas ni Hukbalahap Supremo Luis Taruc, 1954. Punong bayan ng Concepcion, Tarlac, 1955. Pangalawang punong lalawigan ng Tarlac, 1959; punong lalawigan, 1961. Senador, 1967. Ibinilanggo matapos ideklara ang Martial Law ni Pangulong Ferdinand E. Marcos, 23 Setyembre 1972. Hinatulan ng kamatayan ng hukumang militar sa salang subersiyon, ilegal na pag-iingat ng sandata at pagpatay, 1977; pinahintulutang magtungo sa Estados Unidos upang magpagamot. 1980; pinaslang nang bumalik sa Pilipinas, 21 Agosto 1983.
Location Description: The historical marker is located in front of the Ninoy Aquino Monument outside the Benigno S. Aquino Hall in the Pampanga Capitol Compound.

Name: Pampanga Provincial Jail
Address: Pampanga Provincial Jail, San Fernando, Pampanga
Inscription Photo: height: 3238; width: 2332; file: SF (62) Pampanga Jail NHCP Historical Marker.jpg; credit: Ryomaandres {CC BY‑SA 4.0}
Location Photo: credit: Roel Balingit {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; file: Pampanga Provincial Jail historical marker location.jpg; width: 4160; height: 3120
Inscription Tl: Ipinatayo ayon sa disenyo ni William E. Parsons, 1909. Nanatiling bilangguan hanggang inokupahan ng mga puwersang Hapones, 1942–1945. Ibinigay ng Estados Unidos sa pamahalaan ng Republika ng Pilipinas bilang bahagi ng pagtatapos ng Pamahalaang Commonwealth at ipinagpatuloy bilang bilangguan, 1946. Ginamit ang pangalawang palapag bilang tanggapan ng Court of Agrarian Reform at ng Court of First Instance, 1960’s–1970’s; nanatili ang archives section ng Court of First Instance (ngayo’y Regional Trial Court) hanggang 1995. Halimbawa ng arkitektura ng mga panlalawigang bilangguan noong panahon ng mga Amerikano.
Location Description: The historical marker is located at the building facade to the right of the street entrance.

Name: Honorio Ventura
Address: Governor Macario Arnedo Park, Capitol Boulevard, San Fernando, Pampanga
Inscription Photo: height: 2966; width: 2207; file: Honorio Ventura historical marker.jpg; credit: Roel Balingit {CC BY‑SA 4.0}
Location Photo: height: 4160; width: 3120; credit: Roel Balingit {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; file: Honorio Ventura monument.jpg
Inscription Tl: Pilantropo at lingkod bayan. Isinilang sa Bacolor, Pampanga, 30 Hulyo 1887. Nagtapos ng abogasya sa Unibersidad ng Santo Tomas, 1909; hinirang na gobernador ng lalawigan ng Pampanga, 1914. Nahalal nang dalawang termino bilang gobernador ng Pampanga, 1916–1919 at 1919–1921. Kalihim ng Kagawaran ng Panloob matapos ng panunungkulan ni Felipe Agoncillo, 1925–1933. Nagpaaral ng mahihirap na mga mag-aaral kabilang si Diosdado P. Macapagal naging Pangulo ng Pilipinas (1961–1965). Yumao, 3 Setyembre 1940.
Location Description: The historical marker is located in front of the Honorio Ventura monument at the western section of the Gov. Macario Arnedo Park in front of the Capitol building.

Name: Zoilo J. Hilario y Sangalang
Address: Pampanga Provincial Capitol, Capitol Boulevard, San Fernando, Pampanga
Inscription Photo: height: 3602; width: 2781; file: Zoilo Hilario y Sangalang historical marker.jpg; credit: Roel Balingit {CC BY‑SA 4.0}
Location Photo: height: 4160; file: Zoilo Hilario monument.jpg; credit: Roel Balingit {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; width: 3120
Inscription Tl: Mambabatas, makata at tagapagtaguyod ng kagalingang panlipunan. Ipinanganak sa San Juan, San Fernando, Pampanga, 27 Hunyo 1892. Nag-aral para sa titulong batsilyer sa sining, Liceo de Manila, at batsilyer sa batas, Escuela de Derecho. Makatang laureado sa Kastila sa kanyang tulang “Alma Española”, 1917; at makatang laureado sa wikang Pampango sa kanyang tulang “Ing Babai”, 1918. Naglathala ng mga aklat ng tula: Adelfas, Patria y Redencion, Himnos y Arengas at Bayung Sunis. May-akda: Ilustres Varones Filipinos at ng unang “Tenancy Law”, 1932. Kagawad: Philippines Historical Committee at Institute of National Language. Nagharap ng pinakamaraming bilang ng mga panukalang batas na pinagtibay ng Lahislatura ng Pilipinas, 1931–1934. Hinirang na isa sa Sampung Katangi-tanging Mababatas, 1933, at Hukom ng Unang Dulungan, 1951. Namatay, 13 Hunyo 1963.
Location Description: The historical marker is installed upright in front of the monument of Hilario located to the right of the main entrance of the capitol building.

Name: Cabcaben
Address: Bataan Provincial Highway cor. Cabcaben Road, Brgy. Townsite, Mariveles, Bataan
Inscription Tl: Ang limang buwang walang humpay na pagsalakay ng ma Hapon sa Hukbong Pilipino–Amerikano noong Ikalawang Digmaang Pandaigdig ay nagwakas sa isang bahay sa lupang ito sa ganap na ika-5 ng hapon, Mayo 6, 1942 nang bumagsak ang Korehidor at sumuko si Tenyente-Heneral Jonathan M. Wainright ng USAFFE kay Tenyente-General Masaharu Homma, puno ng ika-14 na pangkat ng Hukbong Hapon.

Name: Labanan sa San Rafael
Address: San Juan de Dios Church, San Rafael, Bulacan
Inscription Photo: height: 2893; width: 2350; credit: Photo: Judgefloro; perspective correction: Eugene Alvin Villar (seav); file: Labanan ng San Rafael historical marker.jpg
Location Photo: width: 4608; file: FvfSanRafaelChurchSchool8258 08.JPG; credit: Judgefloro; height: 3456
Inscription Tl: Sa pook na ito naganap noong ika-30 ng Nobyembre 1896 ang isa sa pinakamadugong labanan sa lalawigan ng Bulakan sa pagitan ng mga Katipunero na pinamumunuan ni Heneral Anacleto Enriquez (Matanglawin) at ng mga kawal na Kastila sa pamumuno naman ni Tinyente Koronel Lopez Arteaga. Sa pagkapawi ng usok ng putukan, tinatayang may 800 katao sa panig ng mga Pilipino ang sinamang-palad na namatay kabilang na rito si Matanglawin at iba pang mga Katipunero na nakipaglaban para sa kalayaan hanggang sa huling sandali.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on a concrete mounting in front of the right side of the church facade.

Name: Simbahan ng Angeles
Address: Angeles Church, Santo Rosario Street cor. Santo Entierro Street, Brgy. Santo Rosario, Angeles
Inscription Photo: height: 3789; file: Angeles Church Tagalog historical marker (cropped).jpg; credit: Roel Balingit {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; width: 2632
Location Photo: credit: Roel Balingit {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; file: Angeles Church entrance gate.jpg; width: 4160; height: 3120
Wikipedia Articles: Angeles Church: Holy Rosary Parish Church (Angeles)
Inscription Tl: Dating bisita ng San Fernando. Pinasinayaan ang unang kapilya sa patronato ng Nuestra Señora del Rosario, 1812. Naging ganap na parokya, 1829. Ipinatayo ang simbahang yari sa bato ayon sa disenyo ni Antonio de la Camara, 1877–1896. Dinaluhan ng libo-libong Pilipino ang misang isinagawa dito na sinundan ng talumpati ni Hen. Emilio Aguinaldo bilang bahagi ng pagdiriwang ng unang anibersaryo ng Proklamasyon ng Kalayaan ng Pilipinas, 12 Hunyo 1899. Ginamit ng hukbong Pilipino ang kampanaryo bilang bantayan laban sa hukbong Amerikano, 1899. Nagsilbing ospital at himpilan ng mga Amerikano ang simbahan at kumbento, 1900–1902. Ginamit ng mga Hapon bilang garahe ng mga sasakyang pandigma, 1942. Muling ipinaayos ang loob ng simbahan, 1962.
Location Description: The historical markers are attached to the church patio gate pillars, with the Tagalog marker at the left pillar and the Kapampangan marker at the right pillar.
Inscriptions Other Langs:
pam: Pisamban Maragul, (Pisamban ning Angeles),

Dating bisitas ning San Fernando. Mibuklat ya ing mumunang kapilya kang Nuestra Señora del Rosario, 1812. Megin ganap yang parokya, 1829. Mitalakad ya ing pisamban a yari king batu agpang king disenyu nang Antonio dela Camara, 1877–1896. Tegunan de ring libu-libung Pilipinu ing meganap a misa keti na petukyanan ning metung a talumpati nang Hen. Emilio Aguinaldo antimong metung a dake ning pamagmasusi king mumunang anibersaryu ning Proklamasyun ning Pangatimawa ning Pilipinas, 12 Hunyu 1899. Ginamit de ring ukbung Pilipinu ing kampanaryu antimong batiawan laban karing ukbung Amerikanu, 1899. Megsilbing ospital at himpilan de ring Amerikanu ing pisamban at kumbentu, 1900–1902. Ginamit de ring Hapon bilang garahi karing saken dang pandigma, 1942. Pasibayu yang misamamas ing kilub ning pisamban, 1962.

Name: Mansyong Pamintuan
Address: Pamintuan Mansion, Santo Entierro Street cor. Miranda Street, Angeles
Inscription Photo: width: 2034; file: Mansyong Pamintuan historical marker.jpg; credit: Photo: Judgefloro; perspective correction: Eugene Alvin Villar (seav); height: 3000
Location Photo: height: 3456; file: 1405Pamintuan Mansion Angeles, Pampanga 36.jpg; credit: Judgefloro; width: 4608
Inscription Tl: Ipinatayo ni Mariano Pamintuan noong mga taong 1890. Naging punong himpilan ng Tanggulan ng Republika ng Pilipinas laban sa puwersang Amerikano, Mayo 1899. Nagsilbing pansamantalang tanggapan ni Pangulong Emilio Aguinaldo habang inihahanda ang Tarlac bilang kabisera ng Republika, Hunyo 1899. Sa tapat nito idinaos ang paradang militar noong bisperas ng unang anibersayo ng Proklamasyon ng Kalayaan ng Pilipinas, 1899. Naging himpilan ni Heneral Arthur MacArthur, Agosto 1899. Tahanan ng mga Pilipinong kamikaze ng hukbong panghimpapawid ng Hapon, 1944–1945. Pinaupahan bilang Angeles Hotel, 1948. Binili ni Pedro Tablante mula sa pamilyang Pamintuan, 1959. Naging ekstensiyon ng bahay-pamahalaan ng Angeles, 1964. Binili ng Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas ang lote habang ipinagkaloob ng pamilyang Tablante ang bahay upang ayusin ng pamahalaan, 1981. Isinalin sa Pambansang Komisyong Pangkasaysayan ng Pilipinas, 17 Hunyo 2010. Pinasinayaan ang Museo ng Kasaysayang Panlipunan ng Pilipinas, 24 Agosto 2015.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on a post at the entrance gate to the museum.

Name: Birthplace of Manuel Luis Quezon
Address: Quezon Park, Quezon Street cor. Aurora Street, Baler, Aurora
Inscription En: On this site of this town, Baler, was born Manuel Luis Quezon, 19 August 1878. Indomitable crusader of Philippine independence and social justice, great and fiery statesman, dynamic and far-sighted leader, and true patriot. Son of Lucio Quezon and Maria Molina. Became a soldier in 1899, lawyer, 1903; member, First Philippine Assembly, 1907–1909; Resident Commissioner at Washington, D.C., 1909–1916; President, Philippine Senate, 1916–1935; President, Commonwealth of the Philippines, 1935–1944. Died at Saranac Lake, New York, 1 August 1944.
Inscription Photo: height: 1600; width: 1148; file: Birthplace of Manuel L. Quezon 02.jpg; credit: National Historical Commission of the Philippines
Location Photo: credit: National Historical Commission of the Philippines; file: Birthplace of Manuel L. Quezon 01.jpg; width: 1600; height: 1200

Name: Vicente S. Manansala
Address: Macabebe Municipal Hall, Poblacion, Macabebe, Pampanga
Inscription Photo: width: 3058; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: Vicentejf (cropped).JPG; height: 2530
Inscription Tl: Bantog na pintor at miyuralista. Isinilang sa Macabebe, Pampanga, noong Enero 22, 1910. Nagtapos ng Fine Arts sa Pamantasan ng Pilipinas, 1930. Tagaguhit at lay-out artist ng Philippines Herald, Photo News, Liwayway at Saturday Evening News, Nagwagi ng unang gantimpala ang kanyang “Pounding Rice,” 1940, at “Barung-Barong No. 1,” 1950. Tumanggap ng Outstanding U.P. Alumni Award, 1957; Republic Cultural Heritage Award, 1963; at Araw ng Maynila Patnubay ng Kalinangan Award, 1970. Gumuhit ng miyural “Freedom of the Press,” “Stations of the Cross,” “Agham at Humanidad,” atbp. Ginawaran pagkamatay bilang isang National Artist, 1981. Namatay noong Agosto 22, 1981.

Name: Ang Kabataang Pinuno ng Macabebe
Address: Macabebe Municipal Hall, Poblacion, Macabebe, Pampanga
Wikipedia Articles: Tarik Sulayman: true; Battle of Bangkusay Channel: true
Inscription Tl: Pinamunuan ang mahigit 2,000 mandirigmang Moro buhat sa Macabebe, Hagonoy at iba pang bahagi ng Pampanga para palayasin ang mga Espanyol sa Luzon, 31 Mayo 1571. Hinimok si Lakan Dula ng Tondo na sumama sa kanyang kampanya, ngunit nakapanumpa na ito ng katapatan sa mga Espanyol, kasama sina Raha Matanda at Raha Soliman ng Maynila. Tinanggihan ang alok ni Gob. Hen. Miguel Lopez de Legazpi na pakikipagkaibigan at hinamon ito sa isang labanan sa wawa ng Ilog Bangkusay, Tondo, Look ng Maynila. Napaslang sa naturang labanan, kasama ng 300 iba pang Moro, 3 Hunyo 1571.

Name: Felipe Sonsong
Address: Macabebe Church, Poblacion, Macabebe, Pampanga
Inscription Photo: width: 2871; credit: Judgefloro; file: Felipe Sonsong historical marker (cropped).jpg; height: 4055
Location Photo: height: 4608; file: Macabebe Church patio monuments.jpg; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; width: 3456
Inscription Tl: Isinilang sa Macabebe, Pampanga, 1 Mayo 1611. Lumahok sa Pag-aalsang Maniago, 1660. Naglingkod sa Orden ng mga Misyonerong Agustino sa Pampanga at Misyonerong Dominikano sa Maynila. Napabilang sa Orden ng mga Heswita bilang donado sa Isla ng Marianas, 1668. Nakibahagi sa paggawa ng mga simbahan at bahay ng mga katutubo. Naging tagapagpayo sa mga nangangailangan ayon sa turo ng Diyos. Malubhang nasugatan matapos ang paglusob ng mga rebeldeng katutubo, 23 Hulyo 1684. Nanatili sa Isla ng Marianas hanggang yumao, 11 Enero 1686.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on a concrete mounting at the center of the Macabebe Church patio.

Name: Labanan sa Macabebe
Address: Macabebe Municipal Hall, Poblacion, Macabebe, Pampanga
Inscription Photo: file: Labanan sa Macabebe historical marker 01.jpg; credit: National Historical Commission of the Philippines; width: 1600; height: 1338
Location Photo: width: 1066; credit: National Historical Commission of the Philippines; file: Labanan sa Macabebe historical marker 02.jpg; height: 1600
Inscription Tl: Sinalakay ng mga rebolusyonaryo sa pamumuno ni Hen. Isidoro Torres ang umatras na puwersang Espanyol sa Macabebe, 25 Hunyo 1898. Nakuha ang artileriya ng mga Espanyol, 28 Hunyo 1898.

Name: Simbahan ng Obando
Address: Obando Church, Obando, Bulacan
Inscription Photo: width: 3456; credit: Judgefloro; file: Obando Church historical marker.jpg; height: 4608
Inscription Tl: Ipinatayo ng mga paring Pransiskano sa pangunguna ni Reb. P. Manuel de Olivencia, unang kura ng Obando, noong 29 Abril 1754. Ipinagawa ang pangalawang simbahang bato na may magandang krusero ng mga naninirahan buhat sa buwis na nasingil sa loob ng dalawang taon. Iginuho ng malakas na panganganyon noong Liberasyon ng 1945. Muling ipinagawa ang simbahan at kumbento ng mga taga parokya sa pangunguna ni Reb. P. Marcos C. Punzal sa loob ng dalawang taon. Pinag-ibayo ang pagsasaayos sa pangangasiwa ni D. Reb. Mons. Rome R. Fernandez, H.P. Ipinagdiriwang ang kapistahan ng bayan tuwing ika-17, 18, at 19 ng Mayo bilang parangal kina San Pascual de Bailon, kabilang ang pagsasayaw upang magkaanak; Santa Clara, patrona ng mga naglilihing ina; at Nuestra Señora Virgen de Salambao, patrona ng mga mangingisda at magbubukid.

Name: Simbahan ng San Miguel de Mayumo
Address: San Miguel Church, Libertad Street cor. Victor Street, San Miguel, Bulacan
Inscription Photo: height: 1238; width: 882; credit: National Historical Commission of the Philippines; file: Simbahan ng San Miguel de Mayumo historical marker (cropped).jpg
Wikipedia Articles: San Miguel Church: San Miguel Arcangel Church (San Miguel, Bulacan)
Title Tl: Simbahan ng San Miguel de Mayumo
Inscription Tl: Itinatag ng mga paring Agustino sa patronato ni San Miguel Arkanghel bilang visita ng Candaba, 1607. Naging visita ng Gapan at Macabebe, 1726–1872. Sinimulang itinayo ang kasalukuyang simbahan yari sa bato at ladrilyo sa panunungkulan ni Padre Juan Manuel Tombo, 1848 at natapos sa panahon ni Padre Francisco Arriola, 1869. Naging hiwalay na parokya, 1872. Dito nagkuta ang mga kawal na Espanyol sa ilalim ni Tenyente Telesforo Carrasco noong kasagsagan ng Labanan ng San Miguel de Mayumo, Mayo 1898. Sumuko sila sa mga Rebolusyonaryong Pilipino na pinamunuan ni Koronel Pablo Tecson sa plaza ng simbahan, 1 Hunyo 1898. Napinsala noong Ikalawang Digmaang Pandaigdig at isinaayos sa pangunguna ni Padre Honorio Resurreccion, 1941–1948. Muling kinumpuni, 2003.

Name: Heneral Isidoro D. Torres
Address: Barangay Matimbo Road, Matimbo, Malolos, Bulacan
Inscription Photo: height: 4608; file: General Isidoro D. Torres historical marker.jpg; credit: Judgefloro; width: 3456
Location Photo: height: 3456; width: 4608; file: General Isidoro D. Torres Monument.jpg; credit: Judgefloro
Inscription Tl: Isinilang noong ika-10 Abril 1866 sa baryo ng Matimbo, Malolos; anak nina Florencio Torres at Maria Dayao; nagtapos ng segunda enseñanza sa Kolehiyo ng San Juan de Letran at pagka Batsilyer sa Unibersidad ng Santo Tomas; naging Cabeza de Barangay sa loob ng tatlong taon, 1890–1892; umanib sa Katipunan, 1892, at kilala sa taguring “Matang Lawin”; nakihamok sa iba’t ibang madugong labanan sa Tulay ng Bagbag, Kalumpit, San Rafael, Binakod, at Barasoain, 1896–1899; naging Koronel sa Republika ng Biyak-na-Bato, 1897; kasapi sa Kongreso ng Malolos, 1898; naging Gobernador Militar de la Plaza sa tungkuling Brigadyer, 1898; nagtatag ng gerilya nang ang Malolos ay mapasakamay ni Heneral Arthur MacArthur, ika-31 ng Marso, 1899; juez de paz ng San Antonio, Nuweba Esiha, 1909–1912. Namatay noong ika-5 ng Disyembre, 1928.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on a concrete pedestal at end of an open area marking the birthplace.

Name: Church of Apalit
Address: Apalit Church, Gonzales Avenue cor. Reyes Street, San Juan, Apalit, Pampanga
Inscription En: The Catholic Community of Apalit dates from 1590. The former church, built of brick, was destroyed by the earthquake of 1863. The present Church was constructed by Mariano Santos, of Guagua, under the supervision of the Rev. Antonio Redondo, O.S.A., between 1876 and 1880. Its towers were finished in 1896 by the Rev. Toribio Fanjul, who purposely made them low to minimize the effects of earthquakes.
Inscription Photo: width: 4608; credit: Judgefloro; file: Saint Pedro Apostol Parish Church, Apalit, historical marker.jpg; height: 3456
Location Photo: height: 4608; credit: Judgefloro; file: Saint Pedro Apostol Parish Church, Apalit, right bell tower.jpg; width: 3456
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the church facade, to the right of the main entrance at the bottom of the right bell tower.

Name: Magalang
Address: Magalang–Arayat Road, Magalang, Pampanga
Inscription En: Established by the Augustinians at Macapsa in 1605. Scene of the encounter between the followers of Andres Malong led by Melchor de Vera and the Spanish troops in 1660. Moved to San Bartolome in 1734. Swept by the Parua River in the flood of 1863. Re-established in barrio San Pedro on 13 December 1863 by Gobernadorcillo Pablo M. Luciano. The Revolutionary Government took over, 12 June 1898 until 5 November 1899 when the Americans succeeded. Occupied by the Japanese, 3 January 1942. Liberated by the Americans, 24 January 1945. Turned over to the Republic of the Philippines, 4 July 1946.
Inscription Photo: height: 3000; credit: Photo: Judgefloro; perspective correction: Eugene Alvin Villar (seav); file: Magalang historical marker.jpg; width: 3552
Location Photo: height: 3456; width: 4608; credit: Judgefloro; file: 3513jfSan Nicolas Town Patio Magalang Pampangafvf 09.JPG
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the pedestal holding a sculpture of a book and an eagle at the western side of the town plaza.

Name: Himpilang Pandagat ng Look ng Subic
Address: Subic Spanish gate, Sampson Road cor. Dewey Avenue, Olongapo
Inscription Photo: width: 754; credit: National Historical Commission of the Philippines; file: Naval Base of Subic Bay historical marker 03.jpg; height: 1030
Location Photo: width: 626; credit: National Historical Commission of the Philippines; file: Naval Base of Subic Bay historical marker 02.jpg; height: 428
Wikipedia Articles: Naval Base Subic Bay: U.S. Naval Base Subic Bay
Title Tl: Himpilang Pandagat ng Look ng Subic
Inscription Tl: Isang sentro ng kalakalan bago dumating ang mga Espanyol. Idineklarang daungang pandagat ng Hari ng Espanya, 1884. Sinimulan ang pagpapatayo ng arsenal at istasyong pandagat, 1885. Pansamantalang nakuha ng puwersang Pilipino, 1898. Ngunit napasailalim sa mga Amerikano, 1899. Nasakop ng mga Hapon, 1941 at nabawi ng Amerikano, 1945. Muling pinamahalaan ng mga Amerikano alinsunod sa Military Bases Agreement ng Pilipinas at Estados Unidos, 1947–1991. Nasalanta sa pagputok ng bulkang Pinatubo, 1991. Tuluyang nilisan ng mga Amerikano nang hindi pinagtibay ng Senado ang bagong Military Bases Agreement, 1992. Naging Special Economic and Freeport Zone sa pamamahala ng Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority, 13 Marso 1992.

Name: Simbahan ng Penyaranda
Address: Rizal Street, Peñaranda, Nueva Ecija
Inscription Photo: height: 3456; width: 4608; file: JfSaintFrancisChurchPenarandaNuevaEcijafvf 08.JPG; credit: Judgefloro
Location Photo: height: 4608; width: 3456; file: FvfPenarandaNE0190 19.JPG; credit: Judgefloro
Inscription Tl: Itinayo noong 1869 ni P. Florentino Samonte; ipinagpatuloy ni P. Isidoro Prada ang pagpapagawa, 1873–1875, at ni P Candido San Miguel 1879–1881; at tinapos ni P. Santos Vega, 1887–1889. Ang kumbento na yari sa tisa at kahoy ay itinayo ni P. Valentin Gato de la Fuente, 1889–1891. Ang unang simbahan ay may atip na kugon at pader na bato na itinayo ni P. Alvaro Calleja.
Location Description: The historical marker is located near the leftmost end of the church facade.

Name: Dikaloyungan
Address: Brgy. Zabali, Baler, Aurora
Inscription Photo: height: 1215; width: 843; file: Dikaloyungan historical marker (cropped).jpg; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}
Location Photo: height: 3264; width: 2448; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: Dikaloyungan historical marker.jpg
Inscription Tl: Sa pook na ito noong 3 Setyembre 1897 nagpunit ng sedula ang mga Katipunerong kinabibilangan nina Teodorico Luna Novicio, Antero Amatorio, Norberto Valenzuela, Isabelo Palispis at iba pa at lumagda sa isang manipestong nagpapahayag ng kanilang pagsalungat sa kapangyarihan ng España. Sa pangyayaring ito nagsimula ang Himagsikang Filipino sa Distrito ng Principe (Aurora ngayon). Nagsilbi rin itong himpilan ng Kilusang Rebolusyonaryo sa Baler.

Name: Pook ng Gobierno Militar de la Plaza
Address: Pariancillo Street, Brgy. Sto. Niño, Malolos, Bulacan
Inscription Photo: height: 3013; credit: Photo: Judgefloro; perspective correction: Eugene Alvin Villar (seav); file: Pook ng Gobierno Militar de la Plaza historical marker - 3.jpg; width: 2250
Location Photo: width: 1955; credit: Judgefloro; file: Meralco Malolos branch main entrance.jpg; height: 1752
Title Tl: Pook ng Gobierno Militar de la Plaza
Inscription Tl: Pook na kinatayuan ng kuwartel ni Heneral Isidoro Torres noong itinalaga ang Pamahalaang Rebolusyonaryo at Unang Republika ng Pilipinas hanggang sa Digmaang Filipino–Amerikano, 1898–1899. Dito ipinatayo ang bahay ng mag-asawang Ygnacio Adriano at Gregoria Vasquez, 1916. Hanggang sa mabili ng Meralco bilang sangay sa Malolos, 1995. Isinaayos at pinasinayaan, 21 Mayo 1997. Halimbawa ng estilong Art Nouveau noong unang bahagi ng ikadalawampung dantaon at konserbasyon ayon sa konsepto ng Adaptive Re-use.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the wall to the right of the building main entrance.

Name: Casa Real
Address: Casa Real, Bank of Commerce Road cor. Paseo del Congreso, Malolos, Bulacan
Inscription Photo: height: 879; credit: Ryomaandres {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: CasaReal HistoricalMarker MalolosCity.jpg; width: 570
Location Photo: credit: Judgefloro; file: 2115Malolos Historic Town Center 14.jpg; width: 4608; height: 3456
Inscription Tl: Unang ipinatayong yari sa kawayan at kogon, 1580; pinaayos sa kahoy at nipa noong ika-16 na dantaon. Ipinagawang yari sa bato, 1767; ng ladrilyo at mortar, 1786. Pamuling ipinatayo, 1843. Pinaganda at nagkaroon ng balkonahe, 1918. Naging tanggapan ng gobernadorcillo noong panahon ng Kastila; tesoreriya ng pamahalaang Kastila noong panahon ng pananakop ng mga Ingles sa Maynila; dito nilimbang ang La Independencia, El Heraldo de la Revoluccion, Kalayaan, at Kaibigan ng Bayan. Nasira sa kalaunan at mula sa nalalabing pader at haligi, pinasimulang ayusin at papanumbalikin sa dating kaayusan ang makasaysayang gusaling ito 1980.

Name: Philippine Republic
Address: Malolos Cathedral, Pariancillo Street cor. Estrella Street, Malolos, Bulacan
Inscription En: In this convent, General Emilio Aguinaldo y Famy as President of the First Philippine Republic held office from 10 September 1898 to 29 March 1899.
Inscription Photo: file: MalolosCathedraljf0606 03.JPG; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; width: 4608; height: 3456
Location Photo: width: 3456; file: J1887cMalolosCathedralfvfjr 17.JPG; credit: Judgefloro; height: 4608
Wikipedia Articles: First Philippine Republic: true; Revolutionary Government of the Philippines: Revolutionary Government of the Philippines (1898–1899)
Inscription Tl: Sa kumbentong ito itinatag ang Presidensiya ng Unang Republika Pilipina na pinanguluhan ng Kgg. Emilio Aguinaldo y Famy at dito’y nanatili mula noong ika-10 ng Setyembre 1898 hanggang ika-29 ng Marso 1899.
Location Description: The historical markers are located on the western end of the facade of the convent, beside the cathedral facade.
Inscriptions Other Langs:
es: Republica Filipina, 1898–1901,

En este convento se estableció la Presidencia de la Republica Filipina cuyo Presidente fué Don Emilio Aguinaldo y Famy y lo ocupó desde el 10 de Septiembre de 1898 hasta el 29 de Marzo de 1899.

Name: Simbahan ng Baler
Address: Baler Church, Rizal Street, Poblacion, Baler, Aurora
Inscription Photo: width: 400; credit: Ryomaandres {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: Baler Church in Aurora province historical marker.jpg; height: 588
Location Photo: file: Church facade in Baler, Aurora.jpg; credit: Ryomaandres {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; width: 2592; height: 1944
Inscription Tl:
Unang ipinatayo sa nipa at kawayan ng mga paring Pransiskano sa Tibag (ngayo’y Sabang) sa pagtatangkilik ni San Luis Obispo de Tolosa, 1611. Inilipat sa pamamahala ng mga Rekoletos, 1658; muling ibinalik sa mga Pransiskano, 1703. Nawasak ng daluyong, Disyembre 27, 1735; inilipat sa kasalukuyag kinatatayuan at isang bagong simbahang yari sa bato ang naitayo. Dito, Si Manuel Luis Quezon, unang Pangulo ng Komonwelt ng Pilipinas ay bininyagan, 1878. Isang may 54 kataong garison ng mga Kastila ang kinubkub ng mga Pilipinong rebolusyonaryo, Hunyo 27, 1898 hanggang Hunyo 2, 1899. Napasailalim ng pamamahala ng mga sekular, 1899; muling ipinagawa ng Pangulo at Ginang Quezon, 1939; inilipat sa mga Karmelitas, 1947 at muling ibinalik sa mga sekular, 1983.

Ipinahayag na isang Pambansang Palatandaang Makasaysayan ng Pambansang Suriang Pangkasaysayan Pebrero 29, 2000 sa bisa ng Kautusan ng Pangulo Bilang 260, Agosto 1, 1973, na sinusugan ng mga Kautusan ng Pangulo Bilang 375, Enero 14, 1974 at Bilang 1505, Hunyo 11, 1978.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the left side of the church facade.

Name: Siege of the Church of Baler
Address: Baler Church, Rizal Street, Poblacion, Baler, Aurora
Title En: Siege of the Church of Baler
Inscription En: A Spanish garrison of four officers and fifty men was besieged in this Church by Filipino insurgents from June 27, 1898, to June 2, 1899. Offers of peace and demands for surrender were refused on five occasions. From newspapers dropped into the court by an emissary of General Rios on May 29, the garrison learned for the first time that the Philippines had been lost to Spain and that for many months there had been no Spanish flag in Luzon, except the one waving over Baler Church. Broken by starvation and tropical diseases, the depleted command arranged a truce with the insurgents and marched out of this Church across the mountains to Manila on June 2, 1899. Of the original garrison, two officers, the priest and twelve men had died from disease; two men had been killed by insurgent bullets; two men had been executed; two officers and fourteen men had been wounded; six men had deserted. The fortitude of the garrison was praised by General Aguinaldo in a public document issued at Tarlac on June 20, 1899. Upon their return to Spain the survivors were rewarded by the Queen Regent in the name of Alfonso XIII and the Spanish nation.
Inscription Photo: width: 493; file: Siege of Church of Baler.jpg; credit: Ryomaandres {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; height: 495
Location Photo: file: Church facade in Baler, Aurora.jpg; credit: Ryomaandres {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; width: 2592; height: 1944
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the church facade, to the left of the main entrance.

Name: Lt. Gilmore Rescue Party
Address: Rizal Street cor. San Luis Street, Poblacion, Baler, Aurora
Inscription En: Lieutenant-Commander James C. Gilmore, U.S.N., commanding the U.S.S. Gunboat Yorktown was captured, together with all his command, save two, who were instantly killed and two mortally wounded, by insurgent forces, when he came to Baler in April 1899 to relieve the half-famished Spanish garrison that had been besieged in the town church for nearly a year. Lt. Gilmore and the survivors were taken to Nueva Ecija, and then to Northern Luzon. They were later rescued by American forces and taken to Manila.
Inscription Photo: width: 729; credit: Ryomaandres {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: Lt.GilmoreRescueParty HistoricalMarker Baler.jpg; height: 707
Location Photo: height: 640; credit: National Historical Commission of the Philippines; file: Lt. Gilmore Rescue Party Site historical marker.jpg; width: 480

Name: Corazon C. Aquino
Address: P. Burgos Street cor. F. Tañedo Street, Tarlac City, Tarlac
Inscription Photo: height: 4608; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: Corazon Aquino historical marker in Tarlac City.jpg; width: 3456
Inscription Tl: Ikalabing-isa at unang babaeng Pangulo ng Republika ng Pilipinas, 1986–1992. Isinilang sa Maynila, 25 Enero 1933. Maybahay ni Senador Benigno “Ninoy” Aquino na pinaslang nang bumalik sa Pilipinas matapos ang tatlong taong pamamalagi sa Estados Unidos upang magpagamot, 21 Agosto 1983. Naging pangulo pagkatapos ng 1986 EDSA People Power Revolution. Pinagtibay ang Saligang Batas ng 1987; Family Code ng 1987; Administrative Code ng 1987; at Local Government Code ng 1991. Nilagdaan ang Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Law, 1988. Nalampasan ang ilang pagtatangkang mapabagsak ang kanyang pamahalaan. Yumao, 1 Agosto 2009.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the monument pedestal of Corazon Aquino.

Name: Ang Tahanan ng Pamilyang Aquino
Address: Aquino Ancestral House, F. Timbol Street cor. A. Luna Street, Concepcion, Tarlac
Inscription Photo: file: Aquino Family Ancestral House historical marker in Concepcion, Tarlac.jpg; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; width: 3456; height: 4608
Location Photo: width: 4608; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: AquinoFamilyAncestralHouse-ConcepcionTarlacjf9768 08.JPG; height: 3456
Wikipedia Articles: Benigno Aquino, Sr.: Benigno Aquino Sr.; Servillano Aquino: true; Benigno Aquino Jr.: true
Inscription Tl:
Dito nanirahan ang tatlong henerasyon ng mga tanyag na Filipino: Heneral Servillano Aquino (1874–1959), lumahok sa Rebolusyong Filipino at Digmaang Filipino–Amerikano; Benigno Aquino, Sr. (1894–1947), Ispiker ng Pambansang Asamblea, kinatawan ng Tarlac, senador, at Kalihim ng Agrikultura at Komersyo; at Benigno Aquino, Jr. (1932–1983), punong lalawigan ng Tarlac, senador at lumaban sa rehimeng Marcos.

Ang tahanang ito ay ipinahayag na Pambansang Palatandaang Pangkasaysayan sa bisa ng Board Resolution Blg. 1, s. 1987.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the extreme left portion of the house’s southern facade facing F. Timbol Street.

Name: Teodoro R. Yangco
Address: San Antonio Municipal Hall, T.R. Yangco Street, San Antonio, Zambales
Inscription Photo: credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: Teodoro Yangco Monument & Marker in front of the San Antonio Town Hall in Zambales (cropped).jpg; width: 1816; height: 2582
Location Photo: file: Teodoro Yangco Monument & Marker in front of the San Antonio Town Hall in Zambales.jpg; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; width: 3456; height: 4608
Inscription Tl: Pilantropo at mangangalakal. Isinilang sa San Antonio, Zambales, 9 Nobyembre 1861. Nagtapos sa Ateneo ng Rachiller en Artes at abogasya sa Universidad de Santo Tomas. Nagtapos ng komersyo sa Ealing College, London, 1886. Nagtatag ng sariling kumpanya at pagawaan ng mga barkong pampasahero. May-ari ng Bazaar Siglo XX na bumibili at nagtitinda ng pangkalahatang kalakal. Nanungkulan bilang Filipino Resident Commissioner sa Washington, D.C. 1917–1920, kung saan nakatulong siya sa pagpasa ng batas sa taripang katig sa mga produktong galing sa Pilipinas. Aktibo sa pagsulong sa mga proyektong pangkawang gawa. Presidente ng ilang institusyong pangsibiko tulad ng Young Men’s Christian Association, Kapisanang Laban sa Tuberkolosis, at Gota de Leche. Tinaguriang Ama ng Y.M.C.A. Namatay, 20 Abril 1939.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the monument pedestal in front the municipal hall.

Name: San Antonio
Address: San Antonio Central School, National Highway, San Antonio, Zambales
Inscription En: Explored and settled by Ilocano pioneers from Paoay, Ilocos Norte, 1830. Named Barrio Pamisaraoan, 1836. Became a municipality, 12 May 1849. Witnessed the surrender of the Zambales Spanish forces to the Philippine Revolutionary Army at Annaoangen mountain, June, 1898, and their rout march to the plaza in front of the first Casa Tribunal located on this spot. Occupied by the Japanese, 1942. Liberated by the XI Corps of the Allied Armed Forces that landed at Ua, 29 January 1945.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on a concrete mounting within a separately fenced section of the school perimeter near the street curve.

Name: Penyaranda
Address: Peñaranda Municipal Hall, Brgy. Sinasajan, Peñaranda, Nueva Ecija
Inscription Photo: height: 4608; file: Peñaranda (Nueva Ecija) historical marker.jpg; credit: Judgefloro; width: 3456
Inscription Tl: Sa pamamagitan ng kautusán ng Gobernador Henerál noong 1851, ang nayong Mapisong ng Gapáng ay nagíng munisipyo ng Penyaranda bilang parangál kay José María Peñaranda, inhinyero sibil. Ang mga unang alkalde sa ilalim ng ibá ibáng pamamahala: Basilio Padilla, 1851, panahon ng Kastila; Ponciano Abesamis, 1898–1899, Repúbliká Pilipina; Ambrosio Legaspi, 1900, panahón ng Amerikano; Casiano M. Abes, 1935, Komonwelt; Casiano M. Abes, 1945, Pagkápalaya; Aquilino H. Aberin, 1946, Repúblika ng Pilipinas; Amado B. Ramos, kasalukuyang Alkalde.

Name: Kabisera ng Republika ng Pilipinas
Address: Tarlac State University, College of Computer Studies Building, Romulo Boulevard, Brgy. San Vicente, Tarlac City, Tarlac
Inscription Photo: width: 1928; credit: Ryomaandres {CC BY‑SA 4.0}; file: Kabisera ng Republika ng Pilipinas Tarlac, Tarlac NHCP Historical Marker.png; height: 2824
Inscription Tl: Sa pook na ito dating nakatayo ang Casa Real ng Tarlac na nagsilbing tanggapan ng Pangulo ng Republika ng Pilipinas sa kasagsagan ng Digmaang Pilipino–Amerikano, 21 Hunyo 1899. Dito nilagdaan ni Pangulong Emilio Aguinaldo ang mahahalagang dekreto, kabilang ang pagkilala sa mga huling Espanyol na sumuko sa Baler, 30 Hunyo 1899; itinatag ang Kawanihan ng Salaping Papel, 30 Hunyo 1899; ipinatupad ang Batas sa Pagkamamamayan, 5 Agosto 1899; itinatag ang sistemang koreyo, 29 Agosto 1899; binuo ang Korte Suprema, 15 Setyembre 1899. Lumisan ang pamahalaan bunsod ng pagdating ng puwersang Amerikano, 12 Nobyembre 1899.

Name: Francisco Makabulos
Address: Maria Cristina Park, Romulo Boulevard, Tarlac City, Tarlac
Inscription Photo: height: 4608; file: Francisco Makabulos historical marker in Tarlac City.jpg; credit: Judgefloro; width: 3456
Location Photo: file: FvfTarlacMacabulos9370 02.JPG; credit: Judgefloro; width: 3456; height: 4608
Inscription Tl: Heneral ng Rebolusyon at manunulat. Isinilang sa La Paz, Tarlac, 17 Setyembre, 1871. Nagtatag at nagpalaganap ng Katipunan sa lalawigan ng Tarlac, 1895. Namuno sa Sigaw sa Tarlac, 4 Enero 1897; at pansamantalang pamahalaan sa Gitnang Luzon, 17 Abril 1898. Itinalagang gobernador politico–militar ng lalawigan ng Tarlac matapos palayain ang bayan ng Tarlac, 10 Hulyo 1898. Nanguna sa pagpapalaya sa mga karatig bayan, hinirang na Kumandante Militar ng Tarlac at Pangasinan, 8 Oktubre 1898. Lumaban sa mga Amerikano, 1899; Pangulo ng La Paz, Tarlac, 1908; Pangalawang Pangulo ng Tarlac, Tarlac, 1918. Yumao, 20 Abril 1922.
Location Description: The historical marker is located at the base of the Francisco Makabulos monument.

Name: City of Olongapo
Address: Olongapo City Hall, Rizal Avenue, Olongapo
Inscription En:
Subic Bay, Zambales became a U.S. Naval Station, 1901. Designated as a military reservation was the adjacent land from where a portion of the area grew the community of Olongapo and administered by the U.S. navy officials. Administration of Olongapo was turned over to the Republic of the Philippines by the United States Government, December 7, 1959. By virtue of Executive Order No. 366, Olongapo became a municipality and its local officials appointed.

The desire and aspirations of the citizens of Olongapo led by Mayor James L. Gordon became a fulfillment when Congressman Ramon Magsasaysay, Jr. sponsored H.B. No. 983 converting the municipality of Olongapo into a City. Approved by President Ferdinand E. Marcos, June 1, 1966 as Republic Act No. 4645, and the incumbent elective officials as the first city officials

Name: Provincial Building of Zambales
Address: Zambales Provincial Capitol, Iba, Zambales
Inscription En: This building was constructed by the Spanish Civil Government in the years 1875–1878. The molave and yacal posts were cut in the forest near Dirita. Used as a provincial prison during the Spanish regime, it became the general headquarters of the Revolutionary Government of Zambales in 1899. A portion of the building has, ever since, been utilized as the seat of the Provincial Government. The front part was reconstructed in 1939.

Location Photo: width: 3456; file: IbaCapitoliojf9075 04.JPG; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; height: 4608

Name: Iba
Address: Zambales Provincial Capitol, Iba, Zambales
Inscription En:
Originally the village of Paynaven; founded 1611 by the Recollect Missionaries Fr. Rodrigo de San Miguel and Fr. Andres del Espiritu Santo; formerly situated near Fort Playa Honda; transferred in 1680 by the Dominicans to this site and renamed Iba; later became capital of Zambales. Hometown of Juan Manday, member of Malolos Congress; Silverio Apostol, Acting Secretary of Agriculture, 1922; Gregorio Anonas, representative, 1928–33, manager, Metropolitan Water District, 1934–38 and NDC, 1938–46.

Birthplace of RAMON MAGSAYSAY, President of the Philippines, 1953–·

Location Photo: height: 3456; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: IbaZambalesjf9191 08.JPG; width: 4608

Name: Simbahan ng Hagonoy
Address: Hagonoy Church, Poblacion, Hagonoy, Bulacan
Inscription Photo: height: 2984; credit: Judgefloro; file: Church of Hagonoy historical marker (cropped).jpg; width: 2220
Wikipedia Articles: Hagonoy Church: National Shrine of Saint Anne (Philippines); Hagonoy: Hagonoy, Bulacan
Inscription Tl:
Ang bayan ay itinatag ng mga paring Agustino noong 1581. Yari sa magagaang kagamitan, ang unang simbahan ay ipinagawa sa ilalim ng patronang si Santa Ana. Unang pari nito si Padre Diego Ordoñez Vivar. Pagkaraan, ang simbahan ay binago at ginamitan ng mga bato at ladrilyo, sina Padre Joaquin Martinez Zuñiga, kilalang mananalaysay na Agustino, at Padre Mariano Sevilla, isang malikhaing manunulat na Tagalog, ay naging mga kura paroko ng bayang ito.

Ang simbahan ay ipinaayos noong 1936–1963; binago noong 1968 at inihandog sa Panginoon noong ika 25 ng Hulyo 1970.

Address: Bustos Church, C.L. Hilario Highway, Poblacion, Bustos, Bulacan

Bindoy at Andres upang mahigpit na tutulan ang paghuhulog ng “Juez de Cuchillo”, sa bayang ito. Pinagkasunduan nila na kundi pakikinggan ang kanilang pagtutol ay pagsusunggabanan na lamang nila at sukat ang mga baril at bayoneta ng may apat na raang kasadores na sa kanila ay nakapaligid, at ang palatandaan ng pagsasagawa nito ay ang pagyapos ng mga Kapitang Municipal na taga Bustos sa mga opisyal na Kastila na kanilang kausap sa bulwagan ng tribunal.

Name: Pook na Sinilangan ni Balagtas
Address: Francisco Balagtas Memorial School, Bigaa–Plaridel Road, Brgy. Panginay, Balagtas, Bulacan
Inscription Photo: credit: Judgefloro; file: Balagtas birth place historical marker in Panginay, Balagtas, Bulacan.jpg; width: 3456; height: 4608
Location Photo: height: 3456; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: Balagtas,Bulacanjf9650 33.JPG; width: 4608
Inscription Tl: Dito sa nayon ng Pañginay, bayan ng Bigaá, Bulakán, isinilang si Francisco Balagtas Baltazar, noóng iká-2 ng Abril, 1788. Anák nina Juan Baltazar at Juana de la Cruz. Siya ang kinikilalang Amá ng wikang Tagalog na maykatha ng waláng kamatayang awit na Florante at Laura. Siná José Burgos, José Rizal, Marcelo H. del Pilar, Mariano Ponce, Macario Adriatico, Epifanio de los Santos, Rafael Palma, at ibá pang pantás at bayani ng bansá, ay nagsikilala sa kadakilaan ng nasabing awit ni Balagtas. Namatay siya sa bayan ng Udyong, Bataan, noong iká-20 ng Pebrero, 1862.

Name: Francisco C. Baltazar (Balagtas)
Address: Balagtas Park, Sitio Pag-asa, Brgy. Wawa, Orion, Bataan
Inscription Photo: height: 3354; credit: Photo: Judgefloro; perspective correction: Eugene Alvin Villar (seav); file: Francisco C. Baltazar (Balagtas) historical marker.jpg; width: 2400
Inscription Tl: Makata at manunulat ng ika-19 na siglo. Isinilang sa Panginay, Bigaa (ngayo’y Balagtas), Bulacan, 2 Abril 1788. May-akda ng “Florante at Laura,” 1838 at “Orosman at Zafira,” 1867–1870. Nagbigay inspirasyon sa mga bayani katulad nina Jose Rizal at Apolinario Mabini. Naging kawani ng lokal na huwes sa Maynila, 1840, bago lumipat sa Bataan bilang katulong ng kawani ng korte. Naging unang tenyente at tagapamahala ng taniman at pag-aani sa bayan ng Orion. Yumao, 20 Pebrero 1862.
Location Description: The historical marker is located on the monument pedestal of Francisco Baltazar facing Manila Bay.

Name: Church of Orion
Address: Orion Church, National Road cor. M. Santos Street, Orion, Bataan
Inscription En: The spiritual ministration of Orion belonged formerly with Abucay. Orion became an independent missionary center in 1667. Its first minister was the Rev. Domingo Perez. The Church and the Convent were badly damaged by the earthquakes of September 16, 1852, and were repaired in 1854. The Rev. Ulpiano Herrero constructed the beautiful sacristy and the marble altars. In this town Cayetano Arellano, eminent Filipino jurist and statesman and first Filipino Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, was born on March 2, 1847. Francisco Baltazar Balagtas, author of Florante at Laura, lived in this town from July 22, 1842 to February 20, 1862.

Address: Magsaysay Avenue, Iba, Zambales
Inscription Photo: height: 4608; width: 3456; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: Ramon Magsaysay historical marker at Iba, Zambales.jpg

Inscription Tl: ‘Idolo ng Masa.’ Kilala sa tawag na ‘The Guy.’ Isinilang noong Agosto 31, 1907 sa Iba, Zambales. Nagkamit ng BSC, Jose Rizal College, Mandaluyong, Rizal. Pangkalahatang puno, Zambales Military District, 1942; panghukbong punong-lalawigan ng Zambales at itinaas sa pagka-medyor ni Heneral Douglas MacArthur, 1945; kinatawan, 1946–1950; Pangulo ng Pilipinas, 1953–1957, isa sa mga nagsikap upang mapagtibay ang Rogers Bill para sa mga beteranong Filipino at nagdala nito sa Pilipinas mula sa E.U. Sumupil ng mga Hukbalahap. Nagtatag ng President’s Action Committee (PCAC), National Rehabilitation and Resettlement Administration (NARRA), National Marketing Corporation (NAMARCO), at Land Tenure Administration (LTA). Namatay noong Marso 17, 1957.

Address: President Ramon Magsaysay House, National Highway, Brgy. Sta. Maria, Castillejos, Zambales
Inscription Photo: width: 3456; credit: Ramon FVelasquez {CC BY‑SA 3.0}; file: Ramon Magsaysay Home historical marker.jpg; height: 4608

Ipinamana niya ang mga katangian ng masikap na paggawa, pananagutang sibiko para sa pangkaraniwang tao at makabayang gawain para sa bayan at mga mamamayan.

Muling ipinagawa ng mga inapo ng Pangulong Magsaysay, 1990. Napinsala nang malaki nang pumutok ang Bundok Pinatubo, Hunyo 1991, muling isinaayos ng Pambansang Suriang Pangkasaysayan, 1999.

A contingent of Castillejos residents joined the Revolutionary forces in capturing the Spanish troops in Zambales in 1896. The guerrillas under the command of Ramon Magsaysay dislodged the Japanese soldiers garrisoned at the Castillejos Airstrip on 26 January 1945, in preparation for the liberation of the town four days later.

Address: Abucay Church, Bataan National Road cor. Laon Street, Abucay, Bataan

Nearly two hundred Pampangos were put to death and forty others, together with the Spanish Alcalde Mayor and two Dominican priests were taken prisoners to Batavia. The present Church was badly damaged by the earthquake of September 16, 1852. One of the earliest printing presses in the Philippines was operated in this town, where as early as 1610 Rev. Francisco Blancas de San Jose, O.P., and Don Tomas Pinpin printed several books in Spanish and Tagalog.
